body: **Impact on inflation** Lagging gas prices have risen 53% since the end of February to a peak of $4.56 per gallon last week, driving nominal CPI retail inflation from a five-year low of 2.4% year-over-year (y/y) in February to a three-year high of 3.8% in April. As a result, we raised our forecast for **second quarter of 2026 GDP growth** from 2.5% to 3.0%, while the Blue-Chip consensus raised its estimate from 1.6% to 1.7% (within a range of 0.5% to 2.8%). * Because of the temporary spike in energy prices and the potential for sharply higher nominal inflation to bleed into elevated levels of core inflation over time, we raised our **year-end 2026 estimate for core CPI inflation** from 2.7% to 2.9% (compared with core CPI of 2.8% y/y in April 2026), while the Blue Chip consensus hiked its forecast from 3.2% to 3.4% (within a range of 3.1% to 3.8%).

[The S&P 500](https://www.goldmansachs.com/insights/markets) is forecast to climb 6% to a year-end target of 7,600 (as of April 24), Ben Snider, chief US equity strategist in Goldman Sachs Research, writes in the team’s report. The S&P 500 has surged about 13% since March 30, marking its sharpest rally since April 2020 and, before that, March 2009,[Goldman Sachs Research](https://www.goldmansachs.com/insights/goldman-sachs-research "Follow link")notes. Consensus earnings estimates have risen consistently in recent weeks, reflecting both the limited oil price sensitivity of the S&P 500 and the extraordinary earnings tailwind from spending on[artificial intelligence (AI)](https://www.goldmansachs.com/insights/artificial-intelligence "Follow link").
